text:
All four law families proved across the whole hand-written codec surface: the
wire codecs in AgentDomainJson, the persisted result codecs, the durable control
journal and the transport framing.

Round-trip, malformed-input, unknown-field and bounds laws in
CodecRoundTripLawSuite, CodecMalformedInputLawSuite, CodecBoundsLawSuite,
CodecLawStrengthSuite, ControlCommandJsonLawSuite, JournalReplayLawSuite,
FrameCodecLawSuite and AgentMessageCodecLawSuite. Generators live in core's
Generators, protocol's ProtocolGenerators and managed's ManagedGenerators, with
the hostile-input corpora shared through protocol's JsonCorpus.

Three production defects found and fixed while proving the laws:
- two base64 fields on the agent path decoded before checking their size, and a
  third on the journal path did the same. All now bounded from the encoded length
  before allocating, through one shared helper.
- resultRefs had no cardinality cap.
- LaunchSpec had no round-trip law at all despite three defaulted fields; adding
  it surfaced that a declared-outputs contract must be refused rather than
  silently downgraded to exit-only.

Also verified a security-relevant claim FrameDecoder.readLength documented but
nothing tested: a header with its top bit set is refused as an invalid length
rather than believed.

Every suite carries non-vacuity guards, and the round-trip and chunking laws
carry sensitivity guards that construct the defective implementation the law
exists to rule out and assert the law catches it.

499 tests pass, up from 428 at the start of this line of work.

CARRIED FORWARD, for the codec-ownership work in P6f.12: AgentEnvelope,
AgentBody, ControlCommand and SchedulerQueryResult do not derive CanEqual, so
four law suites supply test-local instances. Whether those public types should
carry structural equality is an API decision, not a law-suite one.
